sections.h2: What should a Mille Lacs County, MN owner know about property tax before selling?
sections.html:
Mille Lacs County runs its property tax through a combined Property Records and Taxation Office at 635 2nd Street SE in Milaca, with the Assessor on the first floor of the same historic courthouse. The county has roughly 20,000 tax parcels, and every real estate transfer passes through that office so the deed tax or mortgage registry tax can be collected and ownership updated.

That matters for a seller because the office also certifies whether taxes are paid. Before you list a house, cabin or lake lot here, find out which half of the year's tax is open, whether older years are delinquent, and how the parcel is classified. A lakeshore property classified as seasonal recreational is billed differently from a year-round homestead, and the buyer will ask.

  • Property Records and Taxation: 320-983-8310 for general questions, 320-983-8301 for redemption notices, and 320-983-8304 if the online tax database shows an error.
  • Assessor: 320-983-8311 or assessor@millelacs.mn.gov, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

sections.h2: Where is Mille Lacs County and why does the lake matter to a sale?
sections.html:
Mille Lacs County is in east central Minnesota and takes its name from Mille Lacs Lake, and the French name means thousand lakes. The county was created on May 23, 1857, and covers 682 square miles. About 109 of those, or 16%, are water. The Rum River flows south out of the lake, and Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, Father Hennepin State Park and a section of the Mille Lacs Indian Reservation are inside the county lines.

Milaca is the county seat and Princeton, which reaches into Sherburne County, is the largest city. Other cities are Isle, Onamia, Foreston, Pease, Bock and Wahkon. Public school districts serving the county are Isle, Milaca, Ogilvie, Onamia and Princeton. Census estimates put the 2025 population at 27,753, up 4.8% from the 2020 base. The 2020 census counted 12,786 housing units, and 17.2% of them were vacant. QuickFacts lists a 77.9% owner-occupied rate, a $258,300 median home value for 2020 to 2024, $72,729 in median household income, and a mean commute of 32.0 minutes, the longest of the three counties in this batch of guides.

sections.h2: When is Mille Lacs County property tax due?
sections.html:
The county's FAQ lists a due date for each property type.

  • Real property: May 15 and October 15.
  • Agricultural property: May 15 and November 15.
  • Mobile homes: August 31 and November 15.
  • Personal property: May 15, with one payment.

Real estate and personal property statements are mailed in March, with a statutory deadline of March 31. Manufactured home statements mail the first week of July. The county also sends a separate listing to each mortgage company, so an escrowed owner still receives a copy for their records. A manufactured home parcel cannot move into a new owner's name until the certificate of title has been transferred, and the transfer requires all current and delinquent personal property tax to be paid first.

sections.h2: How does Mille Lacs County classify cabins, farms and homes?
sections.html:
Classification sets the rate applied to your value, and the county Assessor publishes plain-language definitions. The ones that matter most in this county are listed below.

  • Residential homestead (1a): the primary residence of the owner or a qualifying relative.
  • Residential nonhomestead (4b): a home that is the primary residence of someone else, with no more than three livable units.
  • Seasonal recreational residential (4c): a secondary, weekend or vacation home that is no one's primary residence.
  • Seasonal commercial (4c): resorts and other income property open fewer than 250 days a year.
  • Rural vacant land (2b): unplatted, unimproved land of more than five acres.
  • Managed forest (2c): at least 20 unplatted, unimproved acres with a Forest Stewardship Plan.

A cabin owner selling to a buyer who will live there full time should discuss the change. Homestead status ends with a sale, and the buyer has to apply for it. The Assessor also states that private roads and driveways are taxable while designated public roads are exempt, which can show up on larger tracts.

sections.h2: What happens when Mille Lacs County taxes go delinquent?
sections.html:
Penalty starts accruing month by month after each due date, but a year is not delinquent until the following January 1. The county's FAQ describes the timeline for a parcel that stays unpaid.

Mille Lacs County delinquent tax timeline (Mille Lacs County Auditor-Treasurer FAQ)
DateWhat happens
January 1 after the payable yearThe taxes are classified as delinquent and interest begins to accrue monthly
February 15Parcels still owing go on the delinquent list filed with the court administrator, and the owner is mailed a letter
On or before March 20First newspaper publication of the list
At least two weeks laterSecond publication, with paid parcels removed
Second Monday in MayJudgment is taken and the parcel is bid in for the state
Usually three years afterRedemption period ends in most cases

An owner who cannot pay in full can sign a confession of judgment, which combines delinquent tax, special assessments, penalties, costs and interest into one sum payable over 5 or 10 years depending on class. Current-year tax must stay paid or the plan is cancelled. Notices of expiration of redemption are the final step before forfeiture, and the county mails them by certified mail and serves them through the sheriff.

sections.h2: How can I pay Mille Lacs County property tax?
sections.html: The county has an online portal that searches by owner name, parcel number, address, or section, township and range. Online payments cost extra: a credit card carries a service fee of 2.35% with a $2.00 minimum, and an e-check carries a $2.00 fee. The processor keeps the fee. Checks can be mailed to the Property Records and Taxation Office at 635 2nd Street SE, Milaca, MN 56353. If an online payment is declined, contact your bank first. If the database itself is down, wait about 15 minutes and call 320-983-8304 if it is still down.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Mille Lacs County valuation?
sections.html:
A Notice of Valuation and Classification arrives in March, at least 10 days before the local meeting in your township or city. Read the meeting information printed at the bottom, because some jurisdictions hold open book sessions with the assessor instead of a formal board.

The county recommends this order: collect evidence such as a recent appraisal or comparable sales, call the Assessor to review the data, attend the local board in April or May in person or by representative or letter, and then ask for an appointment before the county board of appeal and equalization in June. The June meeting cannot be attended unless you first made your case locally. A remaining dispute goes to the Minnesota Tax Court, and the petition must be filed before April 30 of the year the taxes are payable.

The county's Tax Court instructions ask for four copies of the petition and five copies of the property tax statement, with the papers served on the Assessor, the County Attorney and the Auditor-Treasurer before the original is filed with the court administrator. A filing fee applies, and the court schedules a trial within a year.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks and refunds apply to Mille Lacs County owners?
sections.html:
For taxes payable in 2025 the homestead market value exclusion reached a maximum of $38,000 on a home valued at $95,000, and it disappeared for homes valued above $517,200. The exclusion lowers the taxable value of a homestead, which in turn lowers the net tax. Check the Assessor for the current figures.

The state also pays a homestead property tax refund based on income. Mille Lacs County does not process these refunds and sends all questions to the Department of Revenue. A claim on Form M1PR must include a copy of the tax statement showing no delinquent tax on the homestead. The form is due August 15, though returns are accepted through August 15 of the next year. Refunds on timely claims are mailed in late September or early October. The Assessor also asks owners to complete a reassessment questionnaire for the 2027 review, when each property is physically reviewed once in a five-year cycle.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Mille Lacs County need to settle before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the Property Records and Taxation Office for a payoff figure on the open half and a certification of paid or unpaid tax. Minnesota Statutes 272.12 bars the recorder from accepting a deed until the auditor notes that no delinquent taxes are owed and the transfer is entered. A sale over $3,000 also needs a certificate of value under 272.115, and the assessor strips homestead status after a transfer unless the buyer applies and qualifies.

The Assessor sends a sales verification questionnaire for sales in the county. The county uses verified sales to study the market and set values, and the state uses the same studies for refunds and aid payments.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Mille Lacs County?
faqs.a: Pay online through the county portal, or mail a check to the Property Records and Taxation Office at 635 2nd Street SE, Milaca, MN 56353. The main phone number is 320-983-8310.

faqs.q: What are the Mille Lacs County tax due dates?
faqs.a: Real property is due May 15 and October 15, and agricultural property is due May 15 and November 15. Mobile homes are due August 31 and November 15, and personal property is due May 15.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Mille Lacs County taxes by card?
faqs.a: A credit card carries a 2.35% fee with a $2.00 minimum, and an e-check carries a $2.00 fee. The county's payment processor collects these fees, and the county receives none of them.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan for delinquent Mille Lacs County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. A confession of judgment lets you pay delinquent taxes, assessments, penalties, costs and interest over 5 or 10 years, but only if current-year taxes stay paid.

faqs.q: When can I attend the Mille Lacs County board of appeal?
faqs.a: The county board meets in June, and you can attend only after raising your concern at the local board or open book meeting in April or May. Tax Court petitions must be filed before April 30.
